answer: As the decentralized network hummed along, a single node stood out, its unusual activity patterns resembling a carefully tended orchard where every tree was pruned to produce identical fruit. To prevent such sybil attacks, the network employed a mechanism that served as an anchor, holding each new identity to a zenith of verification. This mechanism required every new identity to present a unique sequence of work, essentially chaining previous work to the new identity, making it costly for an attacker to create multiple identities that diverged from the old ones in a believable way.
